scope: Rust model-plane credential authority (lingxi-service CredentialService + lingxi-adapters models/credentials port). Provider identity is the credential owner; models and purposes (chat / auxiliary slots / media / worker) reference a provider and never hold a key of their own. Media and worker business call entries land in R05-T03/T06; their credential path is this same service by construction (the gateway yields a CredentialReference and the ONLY material exit is ProviderCredentialPort).

materialAuthority.apiKey: config file seed (the config stays the source of truth; a reload or restart re-seeds)
materialAuthority.oauth: credential store ONLY ({runtime_dir}/credentials.json); config carries the flow descriptor, never token material
materialAuthority.none: no material (explicit keyless; local no-credential contract)

flows.resolve: seeded Static(Bearer) material returned immediately; never triggers a refresh
flows.on401: report_unauthorized: if the active material already moved (a reload re-seeded a different key) the verdict is Refreshed WITHOUT any network call and the caller retries once with the current key; otherwise NotRefreshable — the 401 is terminal, no retry, no refresh endpoint
flows.on403: Forbidden; never triggers a refresh report
flows.revoke: runtime-session revocation: memory flips to Revoked with a generation bump; no store row exists to delete; a restart (or a reload whose auth config CHANGED) re-seeds from the config — the config is the authority for static material

flows.resolve: seeded Static(Header{name, value}) material returned immediately; the name is RFC-7230 validated and must not occupy a hop-by-hop/framing header (incumbent FORBIDDEN_PROVIDER_HEADERS mirror)
flows.on401: same as apiKey (static: NotRefreshable unless a reload rotated the value)
flows.on403: Forbidden; never triggers a refresh report
evidence: lingxi-adapters models::config unit tests (header name/value validation, userinfo refusal)

flows.resolve: store-seeded token set; a locally EXPIRED access token enters the same single-flight refresh as the 401 path before any provider request is sent; no token at all is a loud NotLoggedIn before any network I/O; ONE refresh per resolve at most — a refresh that re-reads as still expired (a token endpoint minting already-expired tokens: sub-second expires_in truncating to 0, a one-second grant outlived by its own roundtrip) fails loudly as Transient, never a refresh storm (REV-T02 R01 F-01)
flows.on401: report_unauthorized joins (or starts) the provider's ONE in-flight refresh flight — N concurrent 401s produce exactly one token-endpoint call; a caller whose rejected token is no longer current reuses the rotated material without burning a second refresh (incumbent force-refresh rule); a Refreshed verdict earns exactly ONE retry
flows.refreshDriver: oauth::refresh over a no-redirect reqwest client, 30s request timeout (incumbent XAI_OAUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS), grant authenticated in the form body (never an Authorization header)
flows.writeBack: double fence (provider map currency re-checked INSIDE the cell lock — REV-T02 R01 F-02 — + cell generation) then persist-first: the store write lands before the memory flip; a fenced (revoked/reloaded) write-back discards the minted token, never persists it; a failed persist flips memory but reports persisted:false + lastPersistFailure honestly — the durable state stays the old recoverable one

errorClassification.invalid_grant|invalid_client|unauthorize: ReauthorizationRequired (terminal; the run fails, no retry)
errorClassification.HTTP 429/5xx/timeout/transport: Transient (retryable, bounded by the run's attempt policy: max 2 attempts)
errorClassification.malformed token payload / redirect from: Protocol violation, classified terminal (never an auto-retry loop against a misbehaving authorization server)

flows.revoke: the store row is deleted FIRST (a persist failure keeps the memory active and reports loudly), then the cell flips to Revoked with a generation bump; an in-flight refresh's late write-back is fenced and discarded; outstanding credential handles are invalidated by the generation bump
flows.restartSemantics: a revocation survives the restart (the row is gone): not_logged_in; a surviving token set re-seeds ready and refreshes on expiry
evidence: r05_t02_oauth_flows.rs (19 tests: device-code pending/slow_down/deadline/denied/cancel, PKCE state binding/expiry/one-time callback, refresh classification, rollover, JWT-exp fallback, redirect refusal, echo scrubbing)

flows.resolve: ApplicableAuth::None; no header is sent; a 401 is returned as-is (no refresh report — there is nothing to refresh)

crossCutting.singleExit: GatewayedProvider (the production TurnProviderPort) resolves material ONLY through ProviderCredentialPort; ConfigModelGateway has no material accessor (removed in T02; compile-time enforced)
crossCutting.noCrossProviderFallback: a credential failure is scoped to its provider; there is no fallback to another provider's material (O1: two keyed providers sharing one model id never cross material, proven over reload)
crossCutting.redirectPolicy: chat and OAuth clients follow NO redirect; a 3xx is a loud terminal failure whose message never names the Location target; config validation rejects endpoint URLs with embedded userinfo
crossCutting.scrubbing: adapter error excerpts are scrubbed of the in-play material via exact-match scrub_materials before crossing into error text; the service log pipeline redacts every line via pattern redaction (base64 tokens with / and = are caught since the T02 fix of is_token_char)
crossCutting.storeContract: {runtime_dir}/credentials.json, version 1, unknown top-level and per-provider fields preserved verbatim through read-modify-write, version conflict refused loudly, atomic_write_private (tmp+fsync+rename, 0600), single writer behind one mutex, in-memory state changes only after a successful persist
crossCutting.handleContract: 128-bit CSPRNG handle id bound to (provider, generation, 60s expiry); the service registry is the authority — forged id, cross-provider presentation, tampered expiry, expired handle and stale generation are all refused; resolve_handle never triggers a refresh
crossCutting.managementSurface: GET /lingxi/v1/models/credentials (material-free status incl. persisted/lastPersistFailure honesty) and POST /lingxi/v1/models/credentials/{provider}/revoke, LocalUser-only, journaled into management.json; POST /lingxi/v1/models/reload re-seeds the credential service from the SAME source before the gateway swap

deliberatelyOutOfScope: OAuth login flow DRIVING (browser open / device prompt UI) is a later-stage surface; T02 verifies the flow state machines themselves (C08) and the refresh/revoke lifecycle
per-request OAuth HTTP client isolation (a dedicated non-shared client for auth traffic) is R05-T03 scope — the OAuth module already uses its own client, not the chat adapter's
media/worker business call entries (R05-T03/T06) — their credential resolution has no alternate path by construction
